properties.description:
* WHAT...East to southeast winds near 20 knots.

* WHERE...Straits of Florida.

* WHEN...In Effect.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
swamped bows at reef tract mooring balls, and dragging anchors.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced boaters, especially those with smaller vessels,
should avoid operating in these conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 1 at 2:54AM CDT until October 1 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Though the possibility for additional heavy rainfall is
unlikely across portions of the area north of the Kansas/Nebraska
state line, the ongoing concern for flooding continues for now.

* WHERE...Portions of north central Kansas, including the following
counties, Jewell, Mitchell, Osborne, Phillips, Rooks and Smith and
Nebraska, including the following counties, Adams, Clay, Fillmore,
Franklin, Nuckolls, Thayer, Webster and York.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At least 2-6+" of rainfall have already fallen across the watch
area so far with potentially 0.5-1" more possible to still fall
for mainly a few north central Kansas areas. Though the threat
for heavy rainfall has come to an end for most of the Nebraska
portions of the watch area, the threat for flooding still
remains. Some areas, especially locations near low-lying/poor
drainage areas or along the banks of some rivers/creeks/streams,
could still see flooding. Even after precipitation comes to an
end, the threat for rising water levels to which some rivers or
streams exceed their banks remains.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 1 at 3:27PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TROPICAL STORM CHOI-WAN MOVING WEST-NORTHWEST AND APPROACHING
ALAMAGAN FROM THE EAST-SOUTHEAST...

.NEW INFORMATION...
A Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for Agrihan in the CNMI.
A Typhoon Watch has been issued for Agrihan in the CNMI.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and recommended
actions for people in the Northern Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for Agrihan in the CNMI.
A Typhoon Watch has been issued for Agrihan in the CNMI.
A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Tinian, Saipan,
Alamagan and Pagan in the CNMI.
A Typhoon Watch remains in effect for Alamagan and Pagan in the CNMI.

A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions, including
winds of 39 to 73 mph, are possible within 48 hours.
A Typhoon Watch means that typhoon conditions, including winds of 74
mph or more, are possible within 48 hours.
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected within 24 hours.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for Tinian and Saipan. Please listen
closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that might be in effect for
your area.

All persons in the Watch areas should review their preparedness plan
and begin to take actions to prepare for conditions as indicated by
your local forecast and additional details, below, for your island.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 2 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) was located
near latitude 16.8N, longitude 147.5E. This was about 290 miles
northeast of Guam. Choi-wan is estimated to be moving west-northwest
at 18 mph, to then slow down to less than 10 mph tonight. The current
forecast speed is likely to be a result of a center position being
farther west than the prior forecast, skewing the forward speed higher
during this cycle. Storm intensity was 45 mph. Choi-wan is forecast
to intensify through tonight, possibly becoming a typhoon Friday
afternoon.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) has increased in forward speed to then
once again slow down later tonight, with a slight contraction in the
tropical storm-force wind field expected to the west and southwest,
but remain well within Tinian, Saipan and their adjacent waters as
Choi-wan comes closer. As such, the Tropical Storm Watch was upgraded
to Tropical Storm Warning for Agrihan, and a new Typhoon Watch
issued as well. Choi-wan will continue west through tonight, making a
turn to the northwest Friday morning as it begins to approach
Alamagan from the south and intensify into a typhoon sometime Friday
afternoon, turning sharply northward, to then move north-
northeastward late Friday night. This forecasted passage along the
axis of the Far Northern Marianas is still expected to prolong the
duration of damaging winds across the northern islands, likely
leading to a lengthy period of time of damaging to destructive
tropical storm conditions beginning this evening and continuing into
Sunday afternoon. As Choi-wan is forecast to strengthen to a typhoon,
there is likelihood for typhoon-force conditions to develop
somewhere along the far Northern Marianas. As such, a Typhoon Watch
and Tropical Storm Warning remain in effect for Alamagan and Pagan.
properties.instruction:
Stay indoors during heavy rain and tropical storm-force wind conditions
associated with Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W). Heed the advice of
your local emergency managers and officials, and continue to monitor
forecasts by the National Weather Service office in Tiyan, Guam.
Remain in sturdy shelter until the all-clear is given.

Take small loose object indoors. Identify suitable shelter. Stock up
a few days worth of food and water. If no concrete shelter is
available, look for a cave or something similar. Take action to
protect food crops or other possessions as appropriate.

.WIND INFORMATION...
Northerly winds of 10 to 15 mph will turn toward the northeast, then
southeast and increase through Friday as Choi-wan moves into the
northern CNMI and strengthens, potentially becoming a typhoon Friday
afternoon as it approaches Agrihan from the south-southwest.
Tropical storm force winds of 39 to 50 mph may begin by Friday.
Depending on the track and intensity, winds may increase to strong
tropical storm-force of 58 to 65 mph early Saturday morning. Typhoon
force winds greater than 74 mph now look to remain just west of
Agrihan at this time.

.COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Surf will initially build to 8 to 11 feet along east-facing reefs
through Friday morning, then spread along north and west-facing reefs
as the center moves north-northeast through the northern CNMI Friday
night through Saturday night, increasing by several feet during this
time. As Choi-wan continues to strengthen, surf will continue to
increase, likely becoming hazardous during the weekend and then
dangerous by early next week. Significant coastal erosion and some
coastal inundation is expected during Choi-wan's passage.

.OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
Periods of rain, widespread heavy showers and scattered thunderstorms
could produce rainfall totals of 8 to 14 inches by early Monday
morning, with up to 20 inches of rainfall possible near the center of
the system.

properties.description:
FFWTOP

The National Weather Service in Topeka has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Cloud County in north central Kansas...

* Until 400 AM CDT.

* At 1155 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Concordia and Jamestown.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

low-water crossings.

continue to move through Winslow and Bird Springs this evening.

Little Colorado River.

expected.

Winslow, Sunrise, Leupp, and Bird Springs.

At 8:00pm MST /9:00pm MDT/ the stage was 17.9 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Crested and falling.

river on route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp will be
within 3 feet of flooding problems. Minor lowland overflow on
right bank at Winslow.
- This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Homolovi State Park Campground, Hunt Park, McHood Park, Standin
on the Corner Park, Sacred Heart Park and Winslow City Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 30 at 9:52PM CDT until October 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
An upper level low over the southwestern U.S. will bring a Pacific
cold front through South-Central Texas. Isolated to scattered showers
and thunderstorms will develop tonight and spread across the area
Thursday. Locally heavy rain is likely. Rainfall totals from tonight
through Friday will be 1-4 inches with isolated amounts up to 8
inches possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Texas, including the following
counties, Atascosa, Bandera, Bastrop, Bexar, Blanco, Burnet,
Caldwell, Comal, Dimmit, Edwards, Frio, Gillespie, Gonzales,
Guadalupe, Hays, Kendall, Kerr, Kinney, Llano, Maverick, Medina,
Real, Travis, Uvalde, Val Verde, Williamson, Wilson and Zavala.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is a potential for life threatening flooding
somewhere in the watch area. Excessive runoff may result in
flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.
Low-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and
flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rainfall totals of 1-4 inches with isolated amounts of 8 inches
are possible.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
San Antonio, Austin, Round Rock, New Braunfels, Cedar Park,
Georgetown, San Marcos, Pflugerville, Medina, Schertz, Kyle, Del
Rio, Eagle Pass, Seguin, Cibolo, Kerrville, Converse, Universal
City, Taylor and Uvalde.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters; Chuuk Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 1 at 12:15PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
The latest forecasts from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) and
numerical guidance continues to strengthen Tropical Storm Choi-Wan
(26W) as it crosses the Marianas sometime this weekend, possibly
stalling or slowing to a crawl as it does so, becoming a typhoon by
the end of the weekend. Choi-Wan is then forecast to turn north and
accelerate somewhat during the early to middle portion of next week
while it continues strengthening, possibly into a major typhoon.

As all of this occurs, the west to southwest monsoon flow already
encompassing northern Palau (mainly near Koror) and western Yap State
will continue strengthening, with sustained winds of 15 to 20 knots
possible. Strong moisture pooling near the trough axis combined with
at least decent surface convergence should foster increasing shower
and thunderstorm coverage and intensity as we head into the weekend
and early next week. Current indications are for 3 to 6 inches of
rainfall, locally in excess of 8 inches being probable for northern
Palau and western Yap State. This could lead to some minor flooding
concerns and landslide potential, especially near Koror where the
steeper terrain is juxtaposed with the strong moisture pooling and
surface convergence.

As the winds increase, and Choi-Wan strengthens, seas and surf will
also increase. This could lead to hazardous conditions for the
northern reefs and potentially for small craft traversing the waters.

Residents across northern Palau and western Yap States are encouraged
to continue to follow forecast trends at www.weather.gov/gum and on
social media.

NWSheadline: INCREASING WINDS, SEAS, SURF, AND HEAVY RAINFALL THROUGH EARLY NEXT WEEK AS CHOI-WAN STRENGTHENS NEAR THE MARIANAS

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...From 7 AM CDT Thursday through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

counties, Fremont, Harrison, Mills, Montgomery, Page, Pottawattamie

Cass, Dodge, Douglas, Gage, Jefferson, Johnson, Lancaster, Nemaha,

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 30 at 6:40PM CDT until October 1 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:

warned area, with additional heavy rain expected to develop
overnight. While rapid rises are not expected due to the intermittent
nature of the rain, significant ponding and flooding in low lying
areas will likely begin or continue tonight.

rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Western Sheridan County in northwestern Kansas...
Thomas County in northwestern Kansas...
Western Gove County in west central Kansas...
Logan County in west central Kansas...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM CDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable. Expect
many areas of slow moving or standing water.

the warned area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Between 1 and 4 inches of rain have fallen. This areal
flood warning replaces the flood advisory that was previously in
effect for the area.

warned area.

Colby, Oakley, Grinnell, Levant, Rexford, Winona, Monument, Gem,

Rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 30 at 3:46PM PDT until October 1 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Now through 5 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.92 ft MLLW) at 2:58 PM
Thursday 10/01. These predictions include up to 0.7 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 30 at 1:02PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
ESFLOT

Waves of rain, and possibly a few thunderstorms, will continue
through Thursday night. High moisture content in the atmosphere will
lead to periods of torrential downpours and the threat for 1 to 3
inches of rainfall on a widespread basis through Thursday night.

Repeated rounds of rain over saturated soils may lead to flooding of
low-lying and poor drainage areas as well as rises on area rivers,
including along the Rock, Fox, DuPage, Des Plaines, and Illinois
Rivers.

This outlook means that elevated water levels and potential impacts
are possible, but not yet certain. Persons should closely monitor
forecasts including the possibility of flood watches, warnings, and
advisories.

Additional statements or outlooks may be issued late tonight.

NWSheadline: Areas of flooding and significant rises in river levels possible through late week

properties.areaDesc: Matagorda Islands; Brazoria Islands; Galveston Island; Bolivar Peninsula
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 30 at 6:38AM CDT until October 1 at 12:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard and away from rocks, jetties, and piers. If
caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK IN EFFECT THROUGH THURSDAY MORNING

* WHERE...A portion of west central Texas, including the following
counties, Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher,
Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Nolan,
Runnels, San Saba, Schleicher, Shackelford, Sterling, Sutton,
Taylor, Throckmorton and Tom Green.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding is possible.

- Multiple rounds of heavy rain are possible through Thursday night
as an influx of tropical moisture arrives. This will coincide
with an approaching upper level low pressure system and an
associated frontal boundary. High precipitable water values will
support efficient rainfall production with this activity. Showers
and thunderstorms capable of producing rainfall totals in the 2
to 4 inch range are forecast across the watch area. Locally
higher amounts of 8+ inches care possible.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
